questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Libya?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Libya on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Libya article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by the Mediterranean Sea to the north, Egypt to the east, Sudan to the southeast, Chad and Niger to the south, and Algeria and Tunisia to the west.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Tripoli?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Libya is Tripoli.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Libya on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Libya on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Libya?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Libya article.

questions.proof: The capital of Libya is Tripoli, which is a port on the sea.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Libya about 1,759,540 square kilometres; Kenya about 581,309 square kilometres; Guinea about 245,857 square kilometres; Slovenia about 20,271 square kilometres.
